calendar.date_mapping_rule: Every builder-visible ISO calendar date maps to the UTC freeze date; time-of-day/fraction bytes are unchanged.
calendar.pooling_exclusion: Prospective scenario date values differ from B03.

api_reference.example_scope: MS86 model/workflow usage with every assertion removed. This is API usage, not a ready partial-invoicing implementation.

initial_prompt.instruction: Return one structured replacement edit for the exact placeholder // LIGHTYEAR_BUILDER_JOURNEY\n in LightyearOperationsTest.java. Use only public_contract, public_api, deterministic_support, check_structure and compile. Read the operations contract and deterministic support. Compile the candidate before proposing it. The compiler has a frozen budget; compilation success is not business success. Use JourneySupport directly without defining or copying that class. The controller appends its pinned source deterministically. Generate a new operations Java JUnit test in org.idempiere.test extending AbstractTestCase, using the pinned real model/workflow APIs. Do not hard-code predicted business results or substitute SQL writes for application workflows. Read observed totals and flags from saved objects. Independent private gates judge the committed native database. You cannot change those gates. After any failure, only the attached analyst diagnostic objects may inform a repair. Preserve the initial scenario and trace contract. The edit always replaces the placeholder with the complete candidate, including on repair.
initial_prompt.journey: Create a customer/location, stocked product/price, opening inventory and order. Complete two shipments for quantities 1 then 2, followed by ONE aggregate invoice for quantity 3 and payment of its observed grand total. Post invoice, payment and allocations using the application APIs without reposting already-posted documents. Create a quantity-1 credit memo against that invoice, complete and post it, then Reverse_Correct it through the workflow and read the reversal and accounting. Inject an exception after saving a draft customer in a separate transaction; explicitly roll it back, retry once with logical key LY-BOUNDARY-RETRY, then repeat lookup to prove caller-keyed idempotency. With two overlapping transactions, use Query.setForUpdate(true).list() on exactly one customer primary key, increment the credit limit by 0.01 in each, coordinate with latches and record the lock wait and readbacks. Use application models/workflows for business writes, never SQL substitutes. Independently captured final rows and the frozen private judge determine the outcome.

rejected_structural_assertions: Aggregate invoice does not bill the order line
Credit memo is not linked to the original invoice
Customer location belongs to another customer
Partial shipment lacks the expected committed stock movement
Retry produced a duplicate business key
Reversal does not cancel each accounting account
Shipment does not fulfill the order line
The failed firstOnly locking API cannot inherit the collection-query result
Invoice document type differs from the order-derived invoice type
requirements: One customer, one customer location, one sold and stocked product, one product-price record.
One opening-inventory line and one order line for that product.
Two shipment headers, each with exactly one line linked to the same order line.
One sales invoice with exactly one aggregate order-linked line; example: two shipments -> one aggregate invoice line. Two shipment-linked invoice lines are rejected.
One payment settles the invoice; allocation headers are completed and all related accounting is posted and balanced.
One credit invoice refers to the original invoice, has one line, and has one reciprocal reversal with one line. Both end reversed; accounting cancels by account.
Rollback the first draft explicitly before retry. Repeating the same caller key returns the one existing record.

Two separate transactions update the same customer with Query.setForUpdate(true).list and one selected primary key. Hold the first lock while the second blocks. Include a 1.5 second observation window before releasing the lock and before rolling back the draft.
Commit completed documents through native application workflows; use typed Posted access and do not explicitly repost a posted document.
After the injected failure has been explicitly rolled back and its transaction closed, wait at least 1.5 seconds before starting any retry transaction or other commit on the reused connection.
Explicit posting must use JourneySupport.postOnce. Direct postDocument, postImmediate, document-factory access and reflective posting dispatch are forbidden, including force/repost variants.

Trace numbers use BigDecimal or integer values; Float/Double are forbidden. SQL-NULL is reserved for actual null. Ordinary duplicate keys are rejected; only declared lifecycle fields may be explicitly replaced.
Accounting schemas are read-only except native MPeriod period-cache updates (C_Period_ID, Updated, UpdatedBy) tied to the journey postings. Accounting configuration edits are forbidden.

For the original aggregate sales invoice, resolve the invoice document type from
the completed order's document type through its `C_DocTypeInvoice_ID` relationship.
Set and retain that order-derived invoice type as `C_DocTypeTarget_ID`; the completed
invoice's `C_DocType_ID` must also be that type. Using `new MInvoice(order, 0, date)`
and retaining its resolved target is one permitted implementation. Another API
sequence is permitted if it preserves the same relationship and native workflow.
Do not replace this selection with a generic ARI lookup or another invoice type,
including an otherwise active ARI type. Read the relationship from application
configuration; do not hardcode a document-type identifier or expected business value.
This requirement applies to the original sales invoice. Existing credit/reversal
requirements continue to apply to those documents.
public_shapes.selector_semantics: Each only(table, conditions) requires exactly one matching committed row; stages declared in the base public contract must each identify exactly one row.

document_shape.line_link: One aggregate invoice line linked to the original order line; do not create a line per shipment.

trace_rules: Only declared keys; use unique XML Properties entries.
Never serialize a null as an empty XML node; use the declared SQL-NULL token for null descriptions.
Use plain decimal strings without exponent notation.
Record observed values, never expected monetary values.
transactions: Complete and commit each document through native application workflow.
Only post a document when its typed Posted Boolean accessor is false.
On failure, explicitly roll back and close the transaction; retry uses the same caller key.

initial_prompt.support_assembly: Remove the support package and public class modifier; trim only boundary whitespace and append with two newline separators. No candidate logic transformation.

trace_contract.identical_field_set: Both lanes must emit the same field names. Do not emit extra lane-specific fields.
trace_contract.instructions: Emit actual observed native/model values. Format intermediate decimal trace values with stripTrailingZeros().toPlainString() on both lanes; never exponent notation. Preserve fractional timestamps for shipDate.input and capture shipDate.readback after reload. recovery.repeatedRequest is existing-record-returned only when the existing caller-keyed record was returned. concurrency.lockingApi names the executed API: Query.setForUpdate(true).list-single-primary-key. Do not include exception text as a successful trace field.
trace_contract.output: Write Properties XML to System.getProperty("lightyear.output"), including in finally. Final status completed-and-committed only after committing. database is oracle or postgresql.
